title: Recover adopter quality routing without an active Contract
outOfScope: Changing profile ordering, path classification, override semantics, or quality target ownership.
Rewriting the immutable WI-03 archive created before Hosted CI exposed this defect.
Treating the failed Hosted run as transient or bypassing required provider checks.

sources.reason: Hosted compatibility evidence shows every installed stack failing because the router requires a base without an active Contract.
The CLI currently rejects an omitted base even though it already collects working-tree and untracked changes relative to HEAD.
The real-stack jobs commit the sample project, install AI Cockpit without starting a Work Item, then invoke make ai-cockpit-quality.
Preserves the original implementation and failed Hosted delivery boundary as immutable predecessor evidence.

riskAssessment.reason: The default installed-adopter quality entrypoint fails across language stacks; the recovery must restore zero-configuration routing without weakening conservative classification.

reasons: This recovery changes the governance router used by every installed adopter quality entrypoint.

executionDecision.reason: Hosted logs identify one deterministic missing-default defect; HEAD is the conservative local base when no Contract or explicit base exists.

preReviewWarnings: Confirm Contract and explicit --base precedence remains unchanged.
Confirm no-Contract routing still includes staged, unstaged, and untracked installation changes.
Confirm the original WI-03 archive remains byte-for-byte unchanged.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: When neither --base nor an active Contract exists, the CLI uses HEAD as the receipt base and classifies staged, unstaged, and untracked paths instead of failing.
An explicit --base and an active Contract baseCommit retain precedence over the HEAD fallback; invalid explicit bases still fail closed.
A clean committed fixture followed by untracked installer-style governance files reproduces the Hosted boundary and passes with Strict dispatch after the fix.
English, Japanese, and Chinese governance-profile documentation explains the no-Contract HEAD fallback without weakening Contract-bound Work Item semantics.
Focused router/adopter tests, source-bound evidence, canonical Strict finish/archive, and replacement Hosted checks pass while the original WI-03 archive remains unchanged.
guidelines: New public APIs must be documented.
Do not import internal modules from other features.

intent.problem: PR #545 Hosted compatibility run 30656653772 proved that installed adopters cannot run make ai-cockpit-quality before starting a Work Item because the new router requires --base or Contract baseCommit. All real and extended stack jobs share the same deterministic failure.
constraints: Preserve the existing explicit --base and active Contract baseCommit precedence.
Use HEAD only when no stronger base evidence exists, so installer-created working-tree paths remain visible.
Do not change profile ordering, classification policy, or quality target composition.
Keep the original WI-03 archive immutable and record the Hosted failure in this adjacent recovery.
intent.rationale: HEAD is the only repository-bound baseline available before an adopter starts its first Work Item; the router already combines HEAD-relative tracked changes with staged, unstaged, and untracked paths, so this fallback restores the intended zero-configuration installed entrypoint without reducing risk.

rawUserRequest: Continue all Work Items through Hosted CI, merge, closure, and cleanup without pausing except for a real human or permission blocker; fix discovered non-converging defects before continuing.

declaredIntent.summary: Recover WI-03 Hosted compatibility by making no-Contract adopter routing use a conservative HEAD baseline.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: An installed adopter has a committed project and uncommitted installer-created governance files but no active Contract.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The router uses HEAD, sees the installer paths, and selects Strict instead of raising a missing-base error.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Add a CLI Git fixture with no --base or Contract and assert receipt base, changed paths, and Strict dispatch.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A caller supplies --base or an active Contract baseCommit.
scenarioCoverage.expected: The supplied or Contract base remains authoritative and HEAD fallback is not used.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Retain existing explicit-base CLI coverage and add precedence assertions where needed.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: A caller supplies an invalid explicit base.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Git inspection fails closed rather than silently falling back to HEAD.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Retain the invalid Git base regression and run it with focused tests.
